questions.prompt: Another member is editing the same post at the same time as you. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Nothing special — keep writing. The editor is genuinely collaborative, so both sets of changes merge live. There is no version to send anyone and nothing to reconcile afterwards.

answers.text: Keep writing — edits merge live and you'll see their cursor
Wait until they're finished so your changes aren't overwritten
Duplicate the post and merge the two versions later
Message them to check out the document first

questions.prompt: Why use the built-in headings, callouts, and quote styles instead of formatting text by hand?
questions.explanation: The public site renders stored structure through its own renderer. Built-in styles are what it knows how to display; hand-formatted text survives the editor but breaks on the live page, usually on mobile.

answers.text: They're what the public site's renderer knows how to display correctly
Hand formatting is slower to type
The AI review panel only reads built-in styles
Custom formatting increases the page's load time

questions.prompt: You have a 6 MB photo from competition. What should you do before inserting it?
questions.explanation: Nothing — images are resized, compressed, and converted on upload. Preparing them by hand wastes your time and usually produces a worse result than the pipeline.

answers.text: Nothing — drop it straight in; it's optimised on upload
Resize it to under 500 KB first
Convert it to WebP manually
Upload it to Drive and link to it instead

questions.prompt: How should you treat the AI review panel's suggestions?
questions.explanation: As a second reader with opinions — some good, some wrong. It has no idea which details carry meaning for the club, and it will confidently suggest cutting exactly those.

answers.text: As a second reader whose suggestions you accept or reject on the merits
Apply all of them — it's tuned to the club's voice
Ignore it; it can't read the draft's context
Only use it for headlines, never for body text

questions.prompt: What is true about publishing a post? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Publishing puts the post on the public internet under the club's name, and it can be scheduled — the scheduler checks every few minutes and publishes at the time you set. It is not officer-gated, and it does not notify sponsors.

answers.text: It makes the post publicly readable by anyone, under the club's name
It can be scheduled for a future time rather than done immediately
It requires an officer to approve before the post goes live
It automatically emails every contact in the CRM
